original_question: A graph is called a cograph if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a path with 4 vertices. A graph is said to be chordal if it has no induced cycles with n vertices for every n ⩾ 4. For a finite group G, the enhanced power graph E(G) is the graph with vertex set G and edges {x, y} for all x ̸= y ∈ G such that ⟨x, y⟩ is cyclic. (a) For a given integer n ⩾ 4, determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) has no induced cycles with n vertices. (b) Determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) is chordal. In(Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18073) we proved that if the enhanced power graph of a given finite group is a cograph, then it is also chordal. Also the finite nonabelian simple groups whose enhanced power graph is a cograph are described, and additional information is obtained on finite nonabelian simple groups whose enhanced power graph has no induced cycles with 4 vertices.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.23 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of arXiv:1401.0300, page 165.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation and, in substance, reproduces Problem 21.23 almost verbatim. It correctly defines cograph, chordal graph, and the enhanced power graph E(G); it correctly restricts the scope to finite nonabelian simple groups; it correctly separates the fixed-n induced-cycle question from the chordal question; and it correctly includes the contextual remark that the 2025 preprint proves that cograph implies chordal, classifies the simple groups with cograph enhanced power graph, and gives additional information for the C4-free case.
missing_details: Make explicit that "determine the set" means classify the relevant finite nonabelian simple groups up to isomorphism.
Replace the phrase "has no induced cycles with n vertices" by the standard graph-theoretic equivalent "contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to C_n" to remove any possible ambiguity.
For the chordal part, spell out the definitional equivalence used in the paper: E(G) is chordal if and only if it has no induced cycle C_m for any integer m >= 4.
If the goal is one stand-alone research question rather than two lettered subparts, combine (a) and (b) into a single classification problem with an "in particular" clause.
refined_question: For each fixed integer n >= 4, classify up to isomorphism the finite nonabelian simple groups G whose enhanced power graph E(G) — the graph with vertex set G in which distinct elements x and y are adjacent exactly when the subgroup <x,y> is cyclic — contains no induced cycle C_n; and, in particular, classify up to isomorphism the finite nonabelian simple groups G for which E(G) is chordal, equivalently, contains no induced cycle C_m for any m >= 4.
equivalent_formulation: The chordal part is equivalently: classify the finite nonabelian simple groups G such that the enhanced power graph E(G) is C_m-free for every integer m >= 4.
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 21.23, not a neighboring or broader problem: the wording, definitions, scope, and the specific contextual note about the 2025 preprint all match that problem on page 165 of the 21st-issue new-problems section. There is no narrower theorem/conjecture in arXiv:1401.0300 to replace it with. The only worthwhile sharpening is stylistic and expository: make the classification "up to isomorphism" explicit, use the standard notation C_n for induced cycles, and fold part (b) into the same stand-alone sentence while preserving exactly the paper's intent. No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier issues arise here; the relevant hidden assumptions are only finiteness of G, nonabelian simplicity, and the fixed-n versus all-n distinction.
